transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what finally pushed me to make this appointment is... it's mostly work stuff. I manage a clinic, so I'm constantly dealing with data. I'll start pulling an EPIC quality report, or I'll sit down in one of our clinic metrics meetings with every intention of tracking exactly what's going on. 

But... oh, actually, speaking of EPIC, they just rolled out this massive system update last week that completely changed the dashboard layout. My coworker Brenda was so furious she was on hold with IT for like an hour, and I had to tell her, 'Brenda, the local help desk didn't design the software, they can't put the buttons back.' People just hate change, you know? My husband is the exact same way whenever they update his phone, he refuses to learn the new menus for months. 

But anyway, what was I... right, the meetings and the reports. I'll be sitting there, and within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far away that I realize I’m just rereading the exact same numbers over and over again. Or I'll be in the metrics meeting and suddenly realize I completely missed the whole point of the discussion. It's just getting really frustrating to deal with.
Have you noticed these concentration problems since childhood or adolescence, or is this a new pattern that started more recently?

Oh, it's definitely not new. Even way back in elementary school, I remember teachers always writing on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I think it was Mrs. Gable in third grade who wrote that first... she was this wonderful older lady who kept a huge collection of those classic yellow hardcover Nancy Drew books in the back of the room. I absolutely loved those. I actually just tried to buy a vintage set on eBay for my niece's tenth birthday last month, but my sister told me not to bother because she only wants Roblox gift cards now. It’s a little sad, honestly. Kids just don't appreciate a good physical mystery book anymore, they just want to stare at their iPads all day. Though I guess I stare at EPIC all day, so maybe I can't really judge. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh! My childhood, right. Yeah, so because I was so all over the place, my mother actually had to sit with me at the kitchen table every single afternoon while I finished my homework. If she didn't physically sit there with me, I would just completely lose track of my assignments, or we'd realize I forgot my textbooks at school again.
Aside from these concentration lapses, do you find yourself worrying excessively about various things—like work, health, or family—more days than not, in a way that feels hard to control?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think I worry any more than the average person does. My husband actually says I'm pretty laid back about most things, except maybe when it comes to organizing the pantry, but that's just because I bought these really nice clear acrylic bins from The Container Store last month. They were having this huge sale, and I just couldn't resist. I spent a whole Saturday reorganizing all the dry goods. It looks like something out of a magazine now, though my husband keeps putting the cereal in the pasta bin, which completely defeats the purpose of the labels I printed. I even bought a special label maker for it, the one with the different fonts... 

Wait, sorry, I'm doing it again. Um, worrying. No, I don't sit around feeling anxious or worrying about things constantly. It's more just the frustration of not being able to focus on what I need to do.
Over the past two weeks or so, have you noticed feeling consistently down, sad, or empty, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

No, I haven't really felt down or anything like that. I still enjoy my weekends and my hobbies. Actually, I just started a new hobby—well, I say started, I bought all the supplies for it. I decided I was going to get into watercolor painting. I saw this woman on Instagram who paints these gorgeous little botanical scenes, mostly ferns and eucalyptus leaves, and she makes it look so incredibly relaxing. So I went to Michaels and bought the good paper, the cold-pressed kind, and this beautiful set of Windsor & Newton paints. The tubes are so tiny, but the cashier told me they last forever. Though honestly, I haven't even opened the packaging yet. They're just sitting on my dining room table next to a pile of mail I keep meaning to sort through. I really need to go through that mail, I think there's a jury duty summons in there somewhere... 

But um, what was the question? Oh, feeling sad. No, no, I feel fine emotionally. Just... scattered, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient demonstrates a longstanding, pervasive pattern of inattentive symptoms—distractibility, losing track of tasks, difficulty sustaining attention in meetings, tangential/disorganized speech, and reliance on external structure (mother supervising homework)—with clear childhood onset (elementary school reports of being 'bright but careless') and current functional impairment at work (missing key points in meetings, rereading reports without absorbing content). Anxiety and depressive symptoms were explicitly denied, making GAD and MDD unlikely. The chronicity, early onset, and characteristic pattern of inattention without hyperactive/impulsive symptoms support a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation.
